Danish Firm Launches New Smart Grid Platform for Electric Utilities

COPENHAGEN, June 12 – Danish technology provider Nordicom Energy unveiled a new smart grid management platform on Wednesday, aiming to improve operational efficiency and support Denmark’s transition to renewable energy in the electric utilities sector.

The platform, called GridSync, is designed to help utilities balance supply and demand, reduce energy losses, and integrate growing amounts of wind and solar power. Company officials said GridSync uses real-time data analytics and machine learning to provide utilities with detailed insights into grid performance and consumer usage patterns.

“Denmark is at the forefront of renewable energy adoption, but this creates new challenges for grid stability,” said Nordicom Energy CEO Lars Mikkelsen at the launch event in Copenhagen. “GridSync empowers utilities to make smarter, faster decisions as they manage fluctuating energy flows from wind farms and rooftop solar.”

The Danish Association of Energy Utilities welcomed the launch, stating that advanced digital tools are becoming crucial as the share of renewables in the national grid approaches 70 percent. “Our members are seeking solutions that offer greater flexibility and resilience,” said association spokesperson Anne Toft. “Platforms like GridSync will play an important role in supporting Denmark’s ambitious climate targets.”

Analysts noted that Denmark’s electric utilities sector faces mounting complexity as distributed energy resources multiply. “As electrification accelerates, there is an urgent need for real-time grid visibility and automated controls,” said Emil Rasmussen, an energy analyst with Jutland Research Partners. “This launch reflects a broader trend in Europe toward digital grid modernization.”

Nordicom Energy said GridSync will be rolled out to several Danish utilities this summer, with plans to expand into neighboring Nordic markets by early next year. The company did not disclose pricing details but said the platform is scalable for both large and small grid operators.
